key_insight: Neurovascular Codes turn EEG features into a shared representation for generating fMRI signals. The approach combines target-specific EEG encoders with a noise-to-signal generative model.
problem_solved: Synthesizing fMRI signals from EEG requires capturing how electrical brain activity relates to different blood-oxygen-level responses across brain targets.
method: Train a separate EEG encoder for each target fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window.
Freeze the encoders, concatenate their hidden features, and project them into a shared Neurovascular Code.
Condition a stochastic interpolant on this code to transform Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a modular approach to cross-modal brain-signal generation that combines specialized feature learning with shared generative conditioning. The provided abstract is incomplete and reports no quantitative results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: EEG window → target-specific encoders → shared Neurovascular Code → generated fMRI signals.

Noise-to-signal illustration showing Gaussian noise transformed under code conditioning.
Brain-region icons paired with illustrative generated fMRI time series.
paper_title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
paper_authors: Yiming Sun, Yifan Wang, Aosong Feng, Yijia Ma, Ben Cheng
